subject: Service provider vs processor language + edge cache retention proposal
messages:
From: Marcel Dupont <marcel@bluehaven.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@bluehaven.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify SP/processor carve-outs & telemetry/cache retention

Camila —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're going through Redwood's standard DPA and our legal team has a couple of close questions before we can sign: primarily around whether certain inference optimizations (edge prefix caching, transient KV caches, aggregated telemetry for SLOs) will be considered a "sale" or otherwise fall outside the Service Provider / Processor carve-out under California privacy law (CCPA/CPRA + applicable state addenda).

High level asks:
- Confirm Redwood's position: do you treat prefix/edge caches and transient KV cache as processing strictly to provide the service (i.e., service provider/processor), and therefore not a "sale"?
- If you retain prefixes or telemetry for performance/debugging, what's the maximum retention you can accept contractually? We would prefer <= 48 hours for any identifiable prompt-prefix data.
- Subprocessor process: can you confirm notification cadence and emergency onboarding procedure?

I've attached an initial redline of the DPA with our suggested changes (Bluehaven_DPA_redline.pdf). If possible, could we have a short call with your privacy engineer and solutions lead this week to resolve?

Best,
Marcel Dupont
Head of Legal — Bluehaven Systems
marcel@bluehaven.com

Attachment: Bluehaven_DPA_redline.pdf (redline stub)

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Marcel Dupont <marcel@bluehaven.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify SP/processor carve-outs & telemetry/cache retention

Marcel — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Looping in Karthik (privacy counsel) and Aditya (solutions) so we can give a combined legal + technical response.

Short answers up front:
- Redwood's default position is that inference, KV/prefix caching for SLOs, and aggregated telemetry are within the Service Provider / Processor role and are not a "sale."
- We're willing to accept a contract commitment for short-lived prompt-prefix retention; 48 hours is reasonable for a scoped carve-out — we might propose a clause that limits retention and indexes usage to per-account debugging/perf scenarios.
- Subprocessor notifications: we maintain a running register and provide 30-day notice for planned changes; emergency onboarding can be done with a shorter notice and an incident escalation path (see attachments).

Next steps we propose:
1) Karthik will send a concise addendum snippet you can drop into your redline that clarifies retention bounds and telemetry definitions.
2) Aditya can share a short tech note describing how the prefix/KV cache works and how telemetry is aggregated and de-identified.
3) If acceptable, schedule a 30-minute call Tues or Wed morning PT to finalize.

I'll attach our standard addendum snippet for review.

Thanks — Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai

Attachment: proposed_addendum_snippet.txt (text stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify SP/processor carve-outs & telemetry/cache retention

Marcel/Camila — following up with the legal wording we think addresses Bluehaven's concerns while keeping our operational flexibility. Below is the snippet K can insert into the DPA; happy to iterate.

--- proposed addendum snippet (text) ---
Definitions: 
"Service Provider" (or "Processor") means Redwood Inference when Redwood processes Personal Data solely on Customer's behalf to provide the services described in the Agreement, including but not limited to model inference, request routing, prefix/KV caching for latency optimization, and telemetry for service quality monitoring.

Telemetry & Aggregation: 
Telemetry means performance, usage, error and system metrics collected by Redwood to operate, maintain and improve the Service. Telemetry shall be collected and stored in aggregated or de-identified form whenever feasible. Telemetry that could reasonably be re-identified will be subject to the retention limits below.

Caching & Retention: 
Redwood may use transient in-memory or edge caching (including prefix caching and KV caches) strictly to optimize response latency and to preserve model context. Any cached prompt prefixes or request-level data used for debugging or replay shall be retained for no longer than 48 hours by default, unless Customer explicitly requests longer retention in writing. Cached data shall be deleted automatically after the retention window, unless required for an ongoing security or legal investigation, in which case Redwood will notify Customer promptly.

No Sale; Use Limitation: 
Redwood represents and warrants that it will not sell Personal Data as defined under CCPA/CPRA and applicable state laws. Redwood will only use the Customer's Personal Data to perform the services described in the Agreement or as otherwise instructed by Customer.

Subprocessors & Notice: 
Redwood will maintain an up-to-date subprocessor register available to Customer via the dashboard and via a shared link. Redwood will provide at least thirty (30) days' notice before engaging a new subprocessor for routine onboarding. For emergency onboarding (e.g., urgent capacity, security patching), Redwood may onboard with shorter notice but will notify Customer as soon as practicable and provide post-onboarding details and mitigations.

--- end snippet ---

Attachments: I attached a recommended redline for the DPA and a short tech note on how the prefix cache is scoped to customer contexts.

If that matches Bluehaven's intent, we can formalize in the DPA.

Karthik
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed_addendum_snippet.txt, redwood_prefix_cache_technote.pdf (stubs)

From: Marcel Dupont <marcel@bluehaven.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@bluehaven.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify SP/processor carve-outs & telemetry/cache retention

Camila/Karthik — appreciate the clear language. Bluehaven is generally comfortable with the approach, but two quick clarifications before we finalize: 

1) Edge CDN/Prefix Cache window: can Redwood confirm operationally the 48-hour cap applies to prefixes that may be mirrored to edge CDN nodes (we understand edge nodes may replicate for performance)? We want the contractual commitment to reflect that mirrored copies are still covered by the same retention.

2) Subprocessor notification: 30 days is fine for planned additions. For emergency onboarding, can we get a written post-event report within 7 days that details the subprocessor, location, and scope? That will satisfy our procurement/audit team.

If you can confirm both items, we'll incorporate the snippet into our redline and send to procurement for signature routing.

Thanks — Marcel
Head of Legal, Bluehaven Systems

Quoted text below:

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 15:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify SP/processor carve-outs & telemetry/cache retention

Marcel — good questions; we can confirm both items:

- Edge cache parity: We will include explicit language stating that any mirrored copies of cached prompt prefixes or transient request-level data that exist on edge or CDN nodes are subject to the same 48-hour maximum retention and deletion obligations. Operationally, our edge replication pipeline is configured to honor the TTL and deletion signals propagated from the origin; we will send Aditya's ops note describing the enforcement mechanism.

- Emergency subprocessor report: Redwood agrees to provide a written post-event subprocessor onboarding report within seven (7) calendar days describing the subprocessor's name, location, purpose, and the mitigations used. If the emergency onboarding is due to a security incident, we will provide the standard incident summary as well.

Next steps:
1) Karthik to prepare a single DPA redline that incorporates the 48-hour mirror language and the 7-day post-event reporting.
2) We will share the current subprocessor snapshot (see attached redwood_subprocessors_snapshot.csv) and a Drive link where Bluehaven can find the live registry.
3) If that looks good, we can move to signature routing.

Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
